LawProactive doesn't practice law; we're a free service that connects injured people in Loma Linda with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened and explain your options. There's no obligation to move forward, and the attorneys in our network only get paid if you recover compensation. Reaching out early can help make sure evidence is preserved while it still tells your story clearly.

whyChoose.title: Why Loma Linda Residents Reach Out Early

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash to file a car accident claim in California, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Acting sooner gives an attorney more room to work.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California allows you to recover damages even if you're partly at fault, but your share of blame reduces your compensation. Anything you say to the other driver's insurer — especially in a recorded statement — can be used to shift more fault onto you.

items.title: No Cap, No Upfront Cost
items.desc: California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning you owe nothing unless they recover money for you.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers often use these statements to find ways to reduce or deny a claim. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my accident happened on I-10 near Loma Linda but involved a Caltrans vehicle?
items.answer: Claims involving government entities, like Caltrans, often carry a much shorter filing deadline — sometimes just six months instead of two years. If a public agency vehicle or roadway may have contributed to your crash, it's worth having this reviewed quickly by an attorney.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and we are not a law firm. Any attorney you're connected with through our network works on contingency, so there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
